topic: Sore legs, and the town already knows
title_jp: {筋肉痛|きんにくつう}と{町|まち}の{噂|うわさ}
context: Friday afternoon: the day after climbing {鷹見岳|たかみだけ}, アルちゃん has aching legs and a scratchy throat and goes to the pharmacy on the shopping street. ハナおばあちゃん, there for her knee patches, has already heard all about his hike.
scene: Sore legs after {鷹見岳|たかみだけ} and a scratchy throat. At the pharmacy you bump into ハナおばあちゃん, who has already heard about your hike.

phrases.jp: {忘れない|わすれない}うちに、{薬|くすり}を{飲んで|のんで}おこう。
phrases.en: I'll take my medicine before I forget.
phrases.note: 〜ないうちに + 〜ておこう: 'let me do it now, before X happens'. Very common when talking to yourself.

phrases.jp: {喉|のど|throat|4}が{痛くて|いたくて}、{咳|せき|cough|3}も{少し|すこし}{出ます|でます}。
phrases.en: My throat hurts, and I'm coughing a bit too.
phrases.note: Symptoms at a pharmacy or clinic: 〜が{痛|いた}い, {咳|せき}が{出|で}る, {熱|ねつ}がある.

phrases.jp: この{薬|くすり}、{飲む|のむ}と{眠く|ねむく}なりますか。
phrases.en: Does this medicine make you sleepy?
phrases.note: The question to ask before buying cold medicine you'll take before work or driving.

phrases.jp: {田中|たなか}さんによると、{明日|あした}は{雪|ゆき}が{降る|ふる}かもしれないそうです。
phrases.en: According to {田中|たなか}さん, it might snow tomorrow.
phrases.note: 〜によると…そうです: the source first, then the news. The neatest way to pass on what someone said.

phrases.jp: {無理|むり|overdoing it|4}しないでね。お{大事|だいじ|take care (to someone ill)|4}に。
phrases.en: Don't overdo it. Take care of yourself.
phrases.note: お{大事|だいじ}に is said only to someone ill or hurt. Pharmacists and doctors say it as you leave.

dialogue_setting: The small pharmacy on the {商店街|しょうてんがい}, Friday afternoon. ハナおばあちゃん is at the counter with a box of knee patches.

dialogue.speaker: ハナおばあちゃん
dialogue.jp: あら、アルちゃん。{鷹見岳|たかみだけ}に{登った|のぼった|to climb|4}んだってね。{恵子|けいこ}さんから{聞いた|きいた}よ。
dialogue.en: Oh, アルちゃん. I hear you climbed {鷹見岳|たかみだけ}. {恵子|けいこ}さん told me.
dialogue.note: 〜んだって = 'I hear that…': the casual way to say you heard some news.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: はい。でも{今日|きょう}は{足|あし}が{筋肉痛|きんにくつう|muscle ache|3}で…。{喉|のど|throat|4}も{少し|すこし}{痛い|いたい}んです。
dialogue.en: Yes. But today my legs are aching… and my throat hurts a little too.

dialogue.speaker: ハナおばあちゃん
dialogue.jp: {町|まち}で{風邪|かぜ}が{流行って|はやって|to be going around|3}るらしいのう。ひどくならないうちに{薬|くすり}を{飲み|のみ}なさい。
dialogue.en: Apparently there's a cold going around town. Take some medicine before it gets worse.
dialogue.note: のう is old-fashioned/regional for ね: {流行|はや}ってるらしいね.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: すみません、{喉|のど|throat|4}の{痛み|いたみ|pain|3}に{効く|きく|to work, be effective|3}{薬|くすり}はありますか。{咳|せき|cough|3}は{出ません|でません}。
dialogue.en: Excuse me, do you have something that works for a sore throat? I'm not coughing.

dialogue.speaker: 薬剤師さん
dialogue.jp: こちらがよく{効きます|ききます|to work, be effective|3}よ。{1日|いちにち}{3回|さんかい}、{食後|しょくご|after meals|3}に{飲んで|のんで}ください。…1000{円|えん}お{預かり|あずかり|to take (and hold)|3}します。
dialogue.en: This one works well. Three times a day, after meals. …Out of 1000 yen.
dialogue.note: 〜円お{預|あず}かりします: what every cashier says when you hand over money, before giving change.

dialogue.speaker: ハナおばあちゃん
dialogue.jp: {天気予報|てんきよほう|weather forecast|4}によると、{今夜|こんや}は{ぐっと||sharply, a lot|3}{冷える|ひえる|to get cold|4}そうじゃ。{早く|はやく}{寝なさい|ねなさい}よ。
dialogue.en: The forecast says it'll get much colder tonight. Get to bed early.
dialogue.note: そうじゃ is old-fashioned/regional for そうだ: {冷|ひ}えるそうだ.

listening.intro: At five o'clock the town loudspeakers crackle on, as you walk home up the slope.
listening.title: {防災無線|ぼうさいむせん}のお{知らせ|しらせ}
listening.place: {鷹ノ原町|たかのはらまち}, town loudspeakers

lines.jp: こちらは{鷹ノ原町|たかのはらまち}{役場|やくば|town office|2}です。{町内|ちょうない|in town|2}で、インフルエンザが{流行って|はやって|to be going around|3}います。
lines.en: This is the {鷹ノ原町|たかのはらまち} town office. Influenza is going around town.

lines.jp: {外|そと}から{帰ったら|かえったら}、{手|て}を{洗いましょう|あらいましょう}。{熱|ねつ}が{出たら|でたら}、{早めに|はやめに|early, in good time|3}{病院|びょういん}へ{行って|いって}ください。
lines.en: Wash your hands when you come home. If you get a fever, go to a clinic early.

listening.question: {熱|ねつ}が{出たら|でたら}、どうしたほうがいいですか。
options: {早|はや}めに{病院|びょういん}へ{行|い}く
{役場|やくば}に{電話|でんわ}する
{薬局|やっきょく}で{薬|くすり}を{買|か}う
listening.explain: {熱|ねつ}が{出|で}たら、{早|はや}めに{病院|びょういん}へ: with a fever, go to a clinic early. Hand-washing is for when you come home.

grammar.form: verb ない-form: + うちに ({忘|わす}れないうちに, {降|ふ}らないうちに) · い-adj: -く + ならないうちに ({暗|くら}くならないうちに, ひどくならないうちに) · set phrase: {知|し}らないうちに
grammar.explanation: Do it now, before something unwanted starts: ひどくならないうちに = before it gets worse. Close to 〜{前|まえ}に, but more urgent. {知|し}らないうちに means 'before I knew it'. Never say {忘|わす}れない{前|まえ}に: {前|まえ}に takes the dictionary form ({忘|わす}れる{前|まえ}に).
mark: ひどくならないうちに

examples.jp: {雨|あめ}が{降らない|ふらない}うちに、{洗濯物|せんたくもの|laundry|4}を{入れよう|いれよう}。
examples.en: Let's bring the laundry in before it rains.

examples.jp: {冷めない|さめない|to get cold (food)|3}うちに{食べて|たべて}ね。
examples.en: Eat it before it gets cold.

examples.jp: {知らない|しらない}うちに、{寝て|ねて}しまった。
examples.en: I fell asleep before I knew it.

quiz.question: {暗く|くらく}＿＿うちに、{帰って|かえって}きてね。
quiz.en: Come home before it gets dark.
quiz.explain: Before it gets dark = while it hasn't yet: {暗|くら}くならないうちに, always the plain present negative.

quiz_more.question: {忘れない|わすれない}＿＿、{電話番号|でんわばんごう}をメモしておこう。
quiz_more.en: Let me note down the phone number before I forget.
quiz_more.explain: After a ない-form you need うちに. {前|まえ}に would need {忘|わす}れる{前|まえ}に.

quiz_more.question: {雨|あめ}が＿＿うちに、{出発|しゅっぱつ}しよう。
quiz_more.en: Let's set off before it starts raining.
quiz_more.explain: 'Before X happens' = X hasn't happened yet: {降|ふ}らないうちに. {降|ふ}るうちに isn't used.

kanji.reading: しょほうせんうけつけ
kanji.where: On the glass door of every pharmacy that fills a doctor's prescription, usually in big red or green letters.
kanji.related: {薬局|やっきょく} = pharmacy; お{薬手帳|くすりてちょう} = your medicine record booklet.
kanji.breakdown: {処方箋|しょほうせん}{受付|うけつけ}: 処方 prescribe (処 deal with + 方 method) + 箋 slip of paper + 受付 reception → 'prescription slips received here'.

tip.title: Pharmacy or drugstore?
tip.body: A {薬局|やっきょく} with {処方箋|しょほうせん}{受付|うけつけ} fills prescriptions; a ドラッグストア mostly sells over-the-counter medicine, snacks and shampoo. Some cold medicines ({第1類|だいいちるい}) can only be sold after the pharmacist explains them, so they're kept behind the counter. Expect questions like 「{眠|ねむ}くなっても{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}ですか」.

challenge.prompt: At dinner {恵子|けいこ}さん frowns: 「アルちゃん、{顔色|かおいろ|complexion|3}{悪い|わるい}わね。{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}？」 Tell her what ハナおばあちゃん said and that you'll sleep early before it gets worse.
challenge.model_answer: ハナおばあちゃんによると、{風邪|かぜ}が{流行って|はやって}るらしいので、ひどくならないうちに{早く|はやく}{寝ます|ねます}。
pieces: ハナおばあちゃんによると、
{風邪|かぜ}が{流行って|はやって}るらしいので、
ひどくならないうちに
challenge.explanation: 〜によると names your source, and らしい marks it as hearsay ({流行|はや}ってる is the casual ている). ひどくならないうちに = before it gets worse. The polite {寝|ね}ます fits talking to your host.
challenge.hint: 〜によると · 〜らしいので · 〜ないうちに

vocab.note: {筋肉|きんにく} muscle + {痛|つう} pain. Typical after sport: {足|あし}が{筋肉痛|きんにくつう}だ.
Often written in kana: のど. {喉|のど}が{渇|かわ}く = to be thirsty.

vocab.en: to be going around; to be popular
vocab.note: For illnesses and trends. As a noun, {流行|りゅうこう} = fashion.
Noun from {痛|いた}い. {痛|いた}み{止|ど}め = painkiller.
For medicine or remedies: 〜に{効|き}く. Same sound as {聞|き}く.
{咳|せき}が{出|で}る = to cough (not する).
On medicine labels. Before meals: {食前|しょくぜん}.
Polite cashier set phrase: 〜円お{預|あず}かりします. To leave something with someone: {預|あず}ける.
Weather or body: {体|からだ}が{冷|ひ}える. Food getting cold is {冷|さ}める.
{無理|むり}しないで: the classic caring line to someone tired or ill.

kanji_study.parts: 疒 sickness radical (a sickbed seen from the side) + 甬, which gives the sound ツウ like 通 → pain running through a sick body.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 病 (illness): both have 疒, but 痛 has 甬 inside and 病 has 丙.

kanji_study.parts: 予 'in advance' (also the sound ヨ) + 頁 head → handing something over ahead of time to someone whose head you trust: entrust.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 頂 (いただく): 預 has 予 on the left, 頂 has 丁.

words.en: to leave in someone's care; to deposit

extras.title: Telling the pharmacist what's wrong
extras.title_jp: {症状|しょうじょう}の{言い方|いいかた}
extras.intro: Short lines that cover most colds and aches.

items.jp: {鼻水|はなみず|runny nose|3}が{止まりません|とまりません}。
{頭|あたま}がずきずきします。
items.note: ずきずき = throbbing pain. ひりひり = stinging, like a sore throat.

extras.title: Passing on what you heard
extras.title_jp: {聞いた|きいた}{話|はなし}の{伝え方|つたえかた}
extras.intro: From gossip to news, casual to polite.

items.note: って: the most casual, between friends and family.

items.jp: {雪|ゆき}が{降る|ふる}んだって。
items.note: んだって: casual, sounds like fresh news.
らしい: from what I've heard or seen, not sure.

items.jp: {予報|よほう|forecast|3}によると、{雪|ゆき}が{降る|ふる}そうです。
items.en: According to the forecast, it will snow.
items.note: によると…そうです: clear source, neutral and polite.
